title: Integrated electrical modeling of circulating tumor cells for enhanced dielectrophoretic trapping and electroporation
task: Optimizing dielectrophoretic trapping and electroporation of circulating tumor cells via integrated computational-experimental platform
key_results: Cell-type-specific optimal electric fields identified: 1–4 kV/cm for CTCs/WBCs, 10–40 kV/cm for platelets; impedance magnitude decreased monotonically with applied voltage (1–25 V across 200 µm gap), with maximum sensitivity in 10–100 kHz range confirming enhanced membrane permeability
comments: The multiphysics approach elegantly captures spatially heterogeneous pore dynamics, though the reliance on THP-1 cells as a proxy for primary CTCs may not fully recapitulate tumor cell heterogeneity in electroporation response.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell-type-specific electric field requirements correlate with cell diameter and membrane charging dynamics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: CTCs/WBCs require 1–4 kV/cm; smaller platelets require 10–40 kV/cm due to higher membrane charging threshold

hypotheses.hypothesis: Increasing applied voltage enhances membrane permeability as evidenced by loss of capacitive behavior
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Progressive suppression of negative reactance and transition from capacitance- to conductivity-dominated transport with increasing voltage

hypotheses.hypothesis: DEP confinement enables spatially precise electroporation with reduced off-target effects
hypotheses.result: Supported by computational prediction of heterogeneous pore dynamics concentrated at hyperpolarized membrane regions

title: Probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis DS109-B11 ameliorates age-related muscle weakness via AMPK activation
task: Identify probiotic strains that enhance skeletal muscle function and resilience through AMPK activation
key_results: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis DS109-B11 increased AMPK phosphorylation in C2C12 myotubes, improved grip strength and motor performance in aged mice, and partially preserved muscle mass in neurogenic atrophy model
comments: The study elegantly connects gut microbiota to muscle homeostasis through AMPK signaling, though the specific bioactive metabolite(s) from DS109-B11 remain unidentified.

model_io.model: C2C12 myoblast differentiation assay in vitro

outputs: gene expression (mitochondrial, oxidative phosphorylation, atrophy, inflammation)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Probiotic-derived factors activate AMPK and enhance myogenic differentiation during muscle development
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; DS109-B11 MCS increased AMPK phosphorylation and enhanced C2C12 myogenic differentiation

hypotheses.hypothesis: AMPK activation mitigates dexamethasone-induced myotube atrophy in vitro
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; DS109-B11 MCS mitigated atrophy in treated myotubes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oral DS109-B11 improves muscle mass and function in aged mice through AMPK-dependent upregulation of mitochondrial function
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; grip strength, motor performance, and myofiber area improved with elevated AMPK phosphorylation and upregulated mitochondrial/OXPHOS genes

title: Classification of fallers in Parkinson’s disease through machine learning based feature analysis
task: Machine learning-based classification of fall risk in Parkinson's disease
key_results: Extra Trees classifier achieves 88% internal and 89% external validation accuracy; identifies three key domains: fear of falling, balance/gait, and autonomic dysfunction
comments: Strong external validation across sites; multidomain approach clinically interpretable but modest sample size for generalization.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integrated clinical and gait features enable reliable identification of PD fallers
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; multidomain approach achieves high accuracy with external validation

title: Advancing target discovery through disease-specific integration of multi-modal target identification models and comprehensive benchmarking system
task: Disease-specific drug target identification and benchmarking
key_results: TargetPro achieves strong predictive performance across 38 diseases; TargetBench 1.0 systematically evaluates target discovery models including LLMs
comments: Addresses critical gap in target validation but relies on existing clinical data; generalization to rare diseases unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Disease-specific models outperform generic approaches for target identification
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; reveals disease-specific patterns requiring tailored detection

title: TMPA-HC: a two-stage heterogeneous multi-population algorithm with cooperative search for high-dimensional feature selection
task: High-dimensional feature selection via heterogeneous multi-population optimization
key_results: TMPA-HC achieves competitive performance with consistent convergence on high-dimensional benchmarks; reduces feature redundancy while maintaining classifier performance
comments: Two-stage design elegantly combines fast filtering with refined wrapper search, though computational gains versus baselines not explicitly quantified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Heterogeneous multi-population cooperative search reduces redundancy in high-dimensional feature selection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; structured exploration-exploitation with elite hybridization improves subset quality

title: Interactive AI assisted pediatric burn assessment based on smartphone images
task: Interactive burn depth assessment from smartphone images via depth regression
key_results: SAM-DR achieves 0.96 Dice score in wound segmentation; interactive thresholding enables burn depth classification comparable to expert clinicians
comments: Clever adaptation of SAM for regression; small annotated dataset (294 images) limits evidence for clinical deployment; inter-rater disagreement quantification helpful.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dense regression on segmentation backbone enables objective burn depth prediction from images
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieves performance comparable to human experts with minimal fine-tuning

title: Effects of hydrodynamic nonlocality on electromagnetic wave propagation and topological properties of magnetoplasmas
task: Analyze topological properties and edge modes in nonlocal magnetized plasmas
key_results: Derived explicit dispersion equations for bulk and edge modes; computed Chern numbers for nonlocal dispersion bands; demonstrated impact of nonlocality on edge mode count and topological protection in Voigt configuration
comments: Theoretical framework is rigorous but lacks experimental validation or numerical simulations of the predicted topological phenomena.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nonlocality affects the number and topological protection of edge modes in magnetized plasmas
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—nonlocal models exhibit different edge mode structure and protection compared to local models

title: Multi-objective optimization for 3D heterogeneous WSN deployment using an enhanced Genghis Khan shark algorithm
task: Multi-objective constrained 3D heterogeneous WSN deployment optimization
key_results: EnMOGKSO achieves best Friedman ranks (HV: 2.04, IGD: 2.38) on CEC 2020; in WSN tasks yields coverage 11–12 and connectivity 7 vs. weaker baselines (coverage 5–7, connectivity 4–5); statistically significant improvements (p<0.05)
comments: Specialized multi-objective evolutionary algorithm with strong empirical validation on benchmarks and practical WSN problems; feasibility-first selection is well-motivated for constraint-heavy domains.

model_io.model: EnMOGKSO (Enhanced Multi-Objective Genghis Khan Shark Optimizer with dual archive and feasibility selection)
inputs: 3D WSN deployment space, K-coverage and C-connectivity constraints

hypotheses.hypothesis: Leader-pursuit dynamics with dual archive and feasibility-first selection improve convergence-diversity balance under tight constraints
hypotheses.result: Confirmed—statistically significant hypervolume and IGD improvements vs. competitors on CEC 2020; higher coverage/connectivity in WSN benchmarks

title: Enhanced cybersecurity threat detection using novel tri-metaheuristic loss functions in generative adversarial networks with adaptive attention preservation for network traffic augmentation
task: Cybersecurity threat detection via tri-loss GAN framework with adaptive attention for network traffic augmentation
key_results: 98.73% accuracy and 0.987 F1-score across seven datasets; 40% energy reduction via adaptive attention; ablation shows 49.4% improvement from class imbalance mitigation, 50.6% from loss combination; cross-dataset transfer 87.45–94.23%
comments: Comprehensive evaluation is undermined by acknowledged limitations: poor infiltration attack recall (16–28%), ground truth verification on only 1.8% of deployment samples, and unclear generalization beyond tested datasets.

model_io.model: GAN with tri-component loss (9 differentiable components: attention, Wasserstein, gradient penalty, hinge, triplet, curriculum, PGD, wavelet, cosine)
inputs: network traffic (NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, CIC-IDS2018, Bot-IoT, CICDDOS2019, CSE-CIC-IDS2018)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Systematic integration of nine loss components with adaptive attention improves cybersecurity detection over baselines
hypotheses.result: Confirmed on tested datasets; cross-dataset transfer and adversarial robustness confirmed; infiltration attacks remain poorly detected

title: Ostrich egg shell as an accurate retrospective dosimeter using electron paramagnetic resonance technique
task: Evaluate ostrich egg shell as a retrospective radiation dosimeter using EPR spectroscopy
key_results: Linear dose-response from 0.3 Gy to 1 kGy (R > 0.999); detection limit 0.21 Gy; <18% signal fading over seven days; energy dependence factor 1.01 for Cs-137/Co-60; UV light insensitivity confirmed
comments: The material shows exceptional sensitivity and temporal stability compared to other biogenic dosimeters, making it practically attractive for both retrospective and monitoring applications.

model_io.model: Ostrich egg shell EPR dosimetry system

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ostrich egg shell exhibits superior dosimetric characteristics (sensitivity, stability) compared to standard egg shell dosimeters
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: detection limit 0.21 Gy exceeds alternatives; <18% fading and UV-robustness demonstrated

title: Experimental verification of DAS vibration response characteristics of equal strength beam under sinusoidal excitation
task: Verify quantitative dynamic strain measurement capability of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) under vibration
key_results: Phase sensitivity coefficient measurement showed 7.3% error vs. theory; response linearity R² ≥ 0.99; spatial strain deviation reduced from 23.4% to 1.7% after gauge-length correction; validated frequency applicability up to 50 Hz
comments: The systematic theory-simulation-experiment validation workflow is rigorous, though the approach is limited to beam structures; generalization to complex 3D structures requires further investigation.

model_io.model: Equal-strength beam under sinusoidal excitation with DAS monitoring

hypotheses.hypothesis: DAS accurately quantifies dynamic strain spatial distribution with theoretically predicted phase sensitivity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 7.3% error in phase sensitivity; 1.7% spatial strain deviation with gauge-length correction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic strain exhibits gradient distribution near natural frequency, deviating from static equal-strain assumption
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: strain gradient (large near fixed end, small near free end) observed near resonance; negligible at low frequencies

title: Long-range structural and magnetic coherence in embedded mesospin metamaterials
task: Realize structurally and magnetically coherent mesospin metamaterials via ion implantation
key_results: Demonstrated spontaneous long-range antiferromagnetic order in as-fabricated Fe-ion embedded Pd films without annealing; observed sharp magnetic Bragg peaks via resonant X-ray scattering confirming structural-magnetic coherence
comments: The embedded-mesospin architecture elegantly avoids lithographic disorder while achieving long-range order, providing a promising platform for spin-photon interactions.

model_io.model: Iron-ion embedded palladium thin film metamaterial

hypotheses.hypothesis: Embedded mesospins develop long-range antiferromagnetic order spontaneously without external treatment
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: as-fabricated arrays show sharp magnetic Bragg peaks evidencing extended order
